After breakfast we head to the small town of Guatapé. Just outside town stands the famous El Peñón de Guatapé rock.

The rock takes its name from two neighbouring towns, El Peñón and Guatapé. It is more than 70 million years old and was first climbed in 1954.

The Indigenous people who lived in the area considered the rock sacred. According to a Tahamí legend, a fish named Batolita saved the people from the wrath of the gods by leaping out of the river and turning into a giant rock.

After the excursion, take an evening flight to Bogotá. On arrival, transfer to **Hotel Novotel Bogota Parque 93** and check in.

The day’s sightseeing and transfers take about **9 hours**.

The transfer from Bogotá to Guatavita takes about **2 hours**.

**Elevation:** around 3,000 m.  
**Average temperatures:** +19 °C by day and +9 °C at night.

We first visit the village of Guatavita, then head to the lake. It lies in the crater of an extinct volcano at an elevation of more than 3,000 metres.

The lake is associated with the legend of El Dorado. According to tradition, Indigenous chiefs covered themselves in clay and gold dust, travelled to the middle of the lake and threw gold objects into the water as offerings to the gods. The lake drew gold seekers, though their searches yielded little of the treasure they expected to find.

The lake is also known for its mountain scenery and emerald-green water.

**Note:** The lake is closed to visitors on Mondays.

We recommend warm, comfortable clothing for this excursion.

Your guide will suggest a restaurant for lunch. **Lunch is excluded from the price.**

The transfer from Guatavita to Zipaquirá takes about **2 hours**.

**Elevation in Zipaquirá:** around 2,600 m.  
**Average temperatures:** +19 °C by day and +10 °C at night.

In the afternoon, we visit Zipaquirá’s main square and walk through the town before heading to the Salt Cathedral.

The cathedral lies more than 170 metres underground. Its walls are about 75% salt. Lighting illuminates carved figures in the dark underground halls.

The cathedral has been described as Colombia’s leading attraction since 2007. Religious services are held here on Sundays.

The complex is part of Parque de la Sal. Visitors can also see a hall with a lake, a mineralogy museum, a cinema and souvenir shops.

Return to Bogotá after the excursion.

**Transfer from Zipaquirá to Bogotá:** around 1½ hours.
